"One of the most powerful supercomputers in Italy will be available to public and private scientific research engaged against coronavirus. It is CRESCO6 infrastructure, operational at ENEA Center of Portici, near Naples, capable of up to 1.4 million billion mathematical operations per second. 'We believe that the supercomputer can give a vital contribution in this crucial moment for our country for research into drugs, vaccines and data processing,' emphasizes ENEA President Federico Testa. 'To date it is already available to the team of researchers from the University of Florence, coordinated by Professor Piero Procacci, who is working on a process to block at the root the replication mechanism of COVID-19 and, therefore, the development of the virus,' adds Testa. HPC CRESCO6 ... is the second computing infrastructure by importance in public sphere in Italy after Cineca and is playing a key role in testing efficacy of compounds under investigation, providing in a few hours a reliable prediction of inhibitory efficacy of such compounds, based on atomistic simulations on thousands of parallel processors. In a few days of testing with Procacci team, at least two compounds with promising characteristics have been identified, one commercially available. After this first phase of structural fine-tuning of obtained compounds, HPC CRESCO6 will be used to try to identify optimal molecular structure for possible specific antiviral drug for COVID-19. Since 2018 CRESCO6 in TOP500... applications: climate change etc. Researchers from public and private institutions who intend to submit request... can write..."
